subject: Epoch-based SLO measurement & tail policy for Hosted API (p50 / p95) - MSA language
messages:

Cc: Mike Jensen <mike.jensen@brightline.com>; legal@brightline.com

Subject: Hosted API SLOs — proposal & a few open points

Hi Tessa / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Brightline is moving quickly and we need to lock the SLO language in the MSA for our pilot. Attached is the draft SLO proposal your team shared (SI-Hosted-SLO-Proposal-v2.pdf) plus a small CSV with the sample epochs we recorded during our proof-of-concept.

Two quick asks before we go to legal:
- Can Redwood confirm how measurement epochs are defined and whether they are aligned to calendar hours or sliding epochs (we prefer epoch-based windows to avoid calendar-bound spikes).
- How do you handle transient outages caused by regional maintenance or cross-cloud peering blips? We need a carveout/exception treatment (transparent and auditable).

Brightline’s internal constraint: we require p50/p95 commitments at the application level (end-to-end) with a clear measurement pipeline and evidence for audits. We also need a process for temporary relief during planned infra maintenance.

Please mark up the redlines docx and point us to any traces/checklists we should capture for evidence.

Best,
Asha Kapoor
Head of Platform Partnerships
Brightline Systems

Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — proposal & a few open points

Asha — thanks for the clear asks and for the sample epochs. Quick replies inline and an ask for a short mutual action plan at the bottom.

1) Measurement epoch model
- Redwood proposes an "epochal" measurement: fixed-length epochs that slide by a configurable step (default: 1 hour epoch sliding every 5 minutes). This reduces sensitivity to boundary effects while letting us identify short but repeated spikes. The epochs in your CSV look similar to what we expect; we’ll normalize to request-level routing tags so measurement maps to application paths.
- We can offer either calendar-hour buckets (hour aligned) or sliding epochs; for this MSA we suggest using epoch-based (sliding) by default with an explicit clause that defines the epoch length, slide, and sample weighting.

2) Regional maintenance & transient blips
- We capture maintenance events in an audit log and exclude them from SLO computation if they are pre-declared maintenance windows or auto-detected network fabric incidents that meet our detection criteria (we share detection signals).
- For cross-cloud peering incidents we recommend a two-step approach: (a) temporary relief via a mutually agreed exception (documented and auto-applied when attribution evidence is provided) and (b) operational runbook to failover traffic to a secondary route where available.

3) Evidence and auditability
- We'll provide a time-series package (per-epoch latency histograms, request counts, and routing tags) and an incident packet for each exception claim. That package can be anchored to a Drive folder (we’ve included a sample link in related_links).

Open clarifying questions:
- Do you need the p50/p95 measured on originating client RTT or on Redwood’s egress-to-model component?
- Is Brightline comfortable with an evidence-first exception window (i.e., exception applied after evidence review) or do you prefer a pre-approved maintenance carveout?

Mutual action plan (proposed):
- Tue 2026-09-02: Redwood to send clean SLO language with epoch definition and exception clause.
- Wed 2026-09-03: Brightline legal to send redlines.
- Fri 2026-09-05: Joint review and finalize MSA SLO exhibit.

I’ve attached a marked-up clause (redlines_slo_clause.docx) and the formal proposal PDF. Ben / Karthik: please add anything technical I missed — specifically on sample weighting and warmup exclusions.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

On Sun, Aug 30, 2026 at 10:25 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Asha — thanks for the clear asks and for the sample epochs. Quick replies inline and an ask for a short mutual action plan at the bottom.

Hi all — adding technical detail so the MSA text is actionable and testable by both sides.

Epochs & sampling (technical notes)
- Epoch definition: we recommend a default epoch length of 1 hour with a slide of 5 minutes (i.e., overlapping epochs). For contract language we can state: "epochs are fixed-length intervals of 1 hour with a 5-minute sliding step; SLOs are computed using weighted request samples within each epoch."
- Sample weighting: requests that hit retries or local backoff are tagged and, by default, excluded from p50/p95 computation unless the customer requests end-to-end measurement. We can provide both flavors but will default to Redwood-side measurement for operational predictability.
- Tail clustering: 95th percentile anomalies that correlate with upstream routing changes are grouped and annotated; if they meet the exception criteria (duration > 3 epochs and confirmed cross-region root cause), they qualify for relief.

Warmup & deployments
- Short-lived warmups after model swaps or cluster scaling (<= 2 epochs) are excluded from SLO calculations. Longer sustained degradations are not excluded unless evidence supports a system-level root cause.

Audit packet contents (for legal):
- Per-epoch histogram (latency buckets), request counts, routing tag map, trace ids for sampled slow requests, and incident detection summary.

If you want, I can draft a tight MSA paragraph this afternoon with the exact thresholds (epoch length, slide, exclusion criteria).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

- For maintenance carveouts: pre-declared maintenance windows (>= 72 hours notice) should be auto-excluded. For emergency and peering incidents we’ll rely on the evidence-first exception path you described.
